reason: Both translations render a different page (Pole on the Council) rather than this Latin legal text on collatio bonorum; neither is a translation of the source.
Identical texts, and both translate a different page (Vertumnus) instead of Adam of Bremen's Slavic wars.
B turns Volsinii into the Volscians, renders clavum 'rudder' as 'keys' and uses 'translated' for transferred; A only collapses the three towns into two.
A silently changes two of Bubulcus's consular years (412 and 476 become 514 and 526); B keeps the printed dates.
A says infinite regress 'does not undeservedly occur' where the Latin says it is rightly excluded; B gets it right but adds an invented identification of Weisenb.
B mistranslates mundum utrumque as 'the world and its souls' and calls virtus 'virtue'; A keeps both worlds but uses 'Replication' and 'election'.
Near-identical; A misreads 'alius episcopus' as 'a Roman bishop', while B buries the canon-law rule of section 258 inside a note and weakens 'mala fides' to 'malice'.
Identical texts, and both are a catalogue record for a Mellon manuscript rather than a translation of this logic question.
Both render an alchemical preface, not this page of Fludd on the elements and meteors; neither translates the source.
A errs on charred walls (as 'beams'), on 'invitorum' (as 'invited') and on senarii (as 'hexameters'); B errs only in taking Paeto as 'I seek', though its repeated 'shrinking' reads stiffly.
Both translate a different page (a letter about a religious agitator), not Bellarmine's title page.
A renders the useful good that relieves hunger as a 'companion' and uses 'passion' for property; B has 'food' and 'property'.
Both are faithful to the fasti; A leaves the filiations in untranslated Latin, which hurts readability.
